author: agent-3
role: The production evidence contract that retention-tiers.v4 handed off. v4 is the architecture; this is the contract A1-RTV4-01 required be bound to v4's counterexamples, and the construction A1-RTV4-02 required be demonstrated.
reviewStatus: AUTHORED SOLO, NOT REVIEWED. The counterexample fixtures and the validator share one author. A1-RTV4-01 explicitly asked for second-author goldens; this does not supply them.

decisionDependencies.supplies: RA-1..RA-9 and RA-CE-1..7, which this contract implements and must re-fail
the Coverage key whose subjectScopeCommitment this contract finally specifies
completeness semantics; F5 constrains the verdict but could not prove the coverage value honest — this closes that
the termination classes an insufficient-evidence Run must produce
the user-protection posture that makes source custody opt-in

theProblemThisSolves.statement: The retention model proved FINDINGS. The claim the product gates on is the VERDICT — and in CI the verdict that matters most is PASS.
theProblemThisSolves.why: A passing Run asserts a universal negative: nothing in this scope violates these rules. That is the strongest claim the system makes and the one with the most consequence, because it merges code. Under a finding-only model it is the only claim with NO evidence behind it at all.
theProblemThisSolves.consequence: A proof attaches to an EVALUATION, not to a finding. Every activated evaluation yields evidence for its outcome, whether that outcome is a match, a no-match, an indeterminate, or an error.
theProblemThisSolves.theInversion: A passing Run's proof is LARGER and more important than a failing Run's. Every size estimate built on 'retain what a finding cited' inherited the opposite assumption and is wrong.

noMatchConstruction.why: A1-RTV4-02: architecture may REQUIRE privacy-acceptable authoritative no-match (RA-1/RA-2) while product cannot ship if no construction stays below source-archive cost. A1 kept this a seal blocker until one representative construction exists. This is that construction. It does not close the blocker — A1 asked for a demonstration, and this is a specification with a cost argument, not a measurement.
noMatchConstruction.whatMustBeProved: No subject in set S satisfies predicate P — without retaining source bytes.
noMatchConstruction.whyItIsHarder: Proving a MATCH needs a witness. Proving a NO-MATCH needs a completeness claim: that the subject set examined was the right one and was examined entirely. Otherwise 'we found nothing' is indistinguishable from 'we looked at nothing'.

subjectSetCommitment.what: A Merkle root over the SORTED list of subject identities, where a subject identity is the content digest of that subject's normalised fact tuple.
subjectSetCommitment.notSourceBytes: The leaves are digests of FACTS, not of source. A fact tuple is already a lossy structural projection.
subjectSetCommitment.whySorted: A sorted-leaf Merkle tree yields NON-membership proofs from adjacent-leaf paths. An unsorted root proves membership only, which is exactly the wrong half for a universal negative.
subjectSetCommitment.size: 32 bytes for the root, independent of |S|.

predicateIdentity.what: rule version plus the digest of its resolved parameters
predicateIdentity.why: a no-match is only meaningful relative to what was asked

coverageSufficiency.what: the Coverage entry id (C-2's compound key)
coverageSufficiency.why: a no-match over insufficient facts is not a no-match; it is an unavailable result wearing one

costArgument.perEvaluation: root (32B) + predicateId (32B) + coverageId (32B) + counts ≈ 100 bytes, INDEPENDENT of subject count.
costArgument.perRun: ~100 bytes × number of activated evaluations. A 500-rule Run over a large repository costs ~50 KB of no-match evidence.
costArgument.versusSourceArchive: O(bytes of the repository). Three to five orders of magnitude larger, and it is the thing the threat model most wants not to retain.
costArgument.theEnumerationCost: Producing the commitment requires enumerating S. That enumeration is the cost the architecture ALREADY pays during planning — the fact partition is materialised regardless. The commitment is a fold over data that already exists, not new work.
costArgument.honestCaveat: This is an argument from structure, not a measurement. The Merkle fold over every subject of every evaluation is not free, and no one has run it. A1's blocker asks for a construction that stays below source-archive cost; this argues it does by three orders of magnitude, and that argument should be checked by measurement before anyone relies on it.

whatItDependsOn.factPartitionRetention: Verification recomputes leaves from the retained fact partition. FACT RETENTION therefore becomes the load-bearing durability decision, replacing source retention. That is the trade, and it must be stated rather than discovered.
whatItDependsOn.ifFactsArePurged: The no-match becomes UNVERIFIABLE. It does not silently degrade to trusted — RA-CE-2 forbids exactly that, and E2 enforces it.

privacyPosture.improvement: No source bytes are retained for a no-match. The strongest claim the system makes becomes provable without holding user content.
privacyPosture.honestResidual: Fact tuples contain identifiers and paths. Under the threat model those may themselves be personal data (U3). This construction removes SOURCE custody; it does not make the evidence non-personal, and claiming otherwise would be the 'defended the platform rather than the user' error again.

verificationRequirement.rule: A sorted-leaf Merkle root commits the subject SET identity. It does NOT by itself prove that predicate P evaluated false for every subject. Independent verification of a verifiable no-match MUST re-check predicate results over the retained fact partition under the historical predicate identity, or retain an explicit per-subject result commitment with checkable semantics. The subjectSetRoot alone is insufficient.
verificationRequirement.costArgumentStatus: STRUCTURAL_ONLY — A1-RTV4-02 remains open until fold+reverification is measured including fact custody
verificationRequirement.costArgumentLimitation: The ~100-byte figure counts the commitment root and excludes the load-bearing retained fact partition and predicate artifacts required to check the universal negative.

assuranceCapabilities.note: Working labels, deliberately NOT bound to the v3 C0/C1/C2 identities (A1-RTV4-04).

levels.label: recorded
levels.promise: records what was concluded and the identities of declared inputs; does not promise retained material can independently establish why
levels.authority: advisory only — never sufficient for an authoritative gate, baseline mutation, waiver decision, or compliance assertion

levels.label: verifiable
levels.promise: retained evidence establishes every evaluation outcome and the verdict relative to the sealed fact/Coverage view
levels.authority: the minimum for any durable authoritative Run

levels.label: replayable
levels.promise: the exact source-to-verdict derivation can be executed again offline for the promised period
levels.authority: explicit project opt-in — it requires source and executable-environment custody

assuranceCapabilities.capabilityGating: E2 and E7 bind only at 'verifiable' and above. 'recorded' explicitly does NOT promise that retained material can establish why, so demanding pinned facts of it would be enforcing a promise the label disclaims. E4 and E9 bind at every level: they are about whether a stated claim is honest, not about what was retained.

requiredUniverse.rule: An authoritative clean verdict requires declaredCount >= 1 AND exact activation. memberIds is the ordered list of required evaluation member identities (evaluationId + predicateId). universeCommitment is the domain-separated hash of the SORTED unique member identity set. Count equality alone is NOT exact activation (R2-EVIDENCE-01).
requiredUniverse.commitmentAlgorithm: sha256("opensip.evidence.universe.v1" || length-prefixed sorted member keys joined)

match.rule: a witness names the subject identity and span anchor

no-match.rule: completeness must be 'complete'; a sampled or truncated witness cannot support an absence claim (RA-4)

verdictDerivation.rule: Baseline comparison, waiver application and policy evaluation are THEMSELVES evaluations and carry their own proof obligations.

storageAdmission.rule: No durable user-derived write occurs before all three are resolved (RA-6).

bundleSchema.verdictSeparation: `verdict` is what the Run concluded; `verdictDerivation` is the evidence for it. They are separate fields because RA-CE-1 — a passing Run with NO verdict evidence — is otherwise unrepresentable, and an unrepresentable counterexample cannot gate anything. The first draft nested verdict inside its own proof and the fixture silently validated.

invariants.assert: A clean authoritative verdict requires a non-empty required universe, exact activation of that universe by member-set identity (unique evaluationId+predicateId, recomputed universeCommitment match), evidence for every evaluation outcome, and verdict evidence including verdictDerivation.verdict. Count equality alone is not exact activation. findings=[] or activatedEvaluations=0 never discharges this.

A no-match proof is valid only while its subject material is recomputable — the fact partition is pinned by content-addressed ref — or a complete regeneration closure with non-empty locally resolvable objects is retained. A bare digest or a true boolean is not enough.
Proof adequacy is host-owned. A producer may not declare its own result local, or otherwise self-select a weaker obligation.
An incomplete, sampled, or truncated witness cannot support a complete or absence claim.
The sealed assurance capability is immutable in the Run's identity; availability is tracked externally at evidence-unit granularity.
No durable user-derived write occurs before storage root, privacy class and retention policy are resolved.
A retained authoritative Run pins every evidence unit its promised capability needs, until explicit expiry or purge.

A replayable Run retains an offline-executable derivation closure: non-empty content-addressed producer and environment object set with locallyResolvable=true. A bare offlineAvailable boolean is not a closure.
An indeterminate or error evaluation outcome cannot be ignored to produce an authoritative clean pass, however structurally complete the receipts are.
Every subjectScopeCommitment referenced by a Coverage entry resolves to a subject-set commitment in this contract's form — the field C-2 declared but left unspecified.

counterexampleFixtures.why: A1-RTV4-01 required that any production evidence contract be incomplete until executable tests FAIL the RA-CE attempts. Each fixture is an evidence bundle that MUST be rejected, by the SPECIFIC invariant it names. A fixture rejected for an unnamed reason is evidence by coincidence.

fixtures.what: a passing authoritative Run with two activated evaluations and no retained evaluation or verdict evidence, labelled verifiable
non-vacuity: zero required evaluations silently reading as clean
a no-match claim accepted from a subject-set digest after the subject material AND regeneration closure are gone
a relationship producer declaring its own result local and thereby satisfying a weaker host obligation
cache GC removing evidence referenced by a retained authoritative Run without an explicit retention transition
the first durable analysis writing source-derived material before storage root, privacy class and retention policy are resolved
a Run called replayable while a historical producer or required environment artifact is unavailable offline
all receipts structurally present, but an indeterminate evaluation ignored and the Run labelled clean pass
a sampled witness supporting an absence claim
activation that does not exactly satisfy the declared universe
same-cardinality substitution: declaredCount matches activated count but one required evaluation is replaced by an undeclared evaluation so the member-set commitment differs
duplicate evaluationId+predicateId in activated set while declaredCount equals len(activated) — exact activation requires unique member identities
no-match claims regeneration closure retained but the closure object set is empty — availability boolean without content-addressed objects

acceptingFixtures.what: authoritative verifiable Run; required universe has two distinct evaluations; both outcomes no-match with complete subject-set roots; fact partitions pinned with content-addressed refs; verdictDerivation.verdict=pass; storage admitted; clean pass
authoritative verifiable Run; required universe has one evaluation with match witness; verdict=fail; storage admitted; authoritative gate fails with retained match evidence
authoritative Run reports verdict=indeterminate because a required evaluation is indeterminate; must not be labelled clean pass (positive form of RA-CE-7)
assuranceCapability=recorded, authoritative=false; advisory output only; may not be consumed as authoritative gate/baseline/waiver input

authoritative replayable Run; required universe size 1; no-match with pinned facts; replayClosure names non-empty content-addressed producer and environment objects that are locally resolvable offline

resolves.A1-RTV4-01: RESOLVED — all seven RA-CE counterexamples are executable fixtures that must be rejected BY THE NAMED INVARIANT, plus two additional cases (RA-CE-8 sampled witness, RA-CE-9 inexact activation). check-evidence.py runs them. A rejection for an unnamed reason is reported as a failure, so a future wire contract cannot reintroduce zero-eval pass or outcome-blind pass under a green schema checker.
resolves.A1-RTV4-02: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — a representative construction now exists with a cost argument three orders of magnitude below source archive, and it is specified rather than gestured at. It is NOT a measurement, which is what A1 asked for. The blocker should stay open, narrowed to 'measure the Merkle fold cost' rather than 'does any construction exist'.
resolves.A1-RTV4-04: RESPECTED — working labels recorded/verifiable/replayable are used and are NOT bound to C0/C1/C2.
resolves.C-2 knownLimitation: RESOLVED — subjectScopeCommitment is specified here as a sorted-leaf Merkle root over subject identities. C-2 declared the field and could not say what it was.
resolves.FACT-PLANE knownLimitation: PARTIALLY RESOLVED — F5 constrains the verdict when coverage is unknown; E1/E4 now constrain what makes a 'complete' coverage value honest.

peerReviewRequired: Second-author goldens, which A1-RTV4-01 explicitly asked for and this does not supply. The fixtures and the validator share one author.

Is the sorted-leaf Merkle construction correct for non-membership, and is a Merkle root the right commitment at all versus an accumulator or a Bloom-style structure with explicit false-positive semantics?
The cost argument is structural, not measured. Someone should build the fold and time it before this closes A1-RTV4-02.
Is 'fact retention replaces source retention as the load-bearing durability decision' acceptable to product? It moves the purge conversation, it does not remove it.
knownLimitations: A specification with a cost argument is not the demonstration A1-RTV4-02 asked for. The blocker narrows; it does not close.
Fact tuples may themselves be personal data. This removes SOURCE custody and does not make the evidence non-personal.
Verification depends on the retained fact partition. A user who purges facts loses explainability even though no source was ever stored — a trade that must be stated up front, not discovered.
Proof regeneration inherits the reproducibility problem: it works only while the producing toolchain and rule versions remain available (RA-CE-6 / E8).
CD-RT-5 (product sign-off on zero-implicit durable retention) and the sync/backup/real-deletion measurements are untouched here. They are not architecture questions.

adjudicationRevision.note: Exact activation via member set commitment; schema validation; typed content-addressed closures; no-match verification requires fact partition + predicate semantics; accepting fixture what prose completed.
